name: Question 3
problem: The second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)={e}^{-{x}^{2}}$ about $x=1$ is
worked_solution:
To find the second-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=1,$ we plug $a=1$ into the general formula to give

$$
{P}_{2}(x)=f(1)+{f}^{′}(1)(x-1)+\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(1)(x-1)^{2}.
$$

So, we need to work out $f(1),$ ${f}^{′}(1),$ and ${f}^{″}(1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={e}^{-{x}^{2}} & ⟹ &  & f(1) & ={e}^{-1} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\,2x{e}^{-{x}^{2}} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(1) & =-2{e}^{-1} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =(4{x}^{2}-2){e}^{-{x}^{2}} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(1) & =2{e}^{-1}\end{aligned}
$$

We now plug the results for $f(1),$ ${f}^{′}(1),$ and ${f}^{″}(1)$ into our second-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & ={e}^{-1}+(-2{e}^{-1})\cdot (x-1)+(2{e}^{-1})\cdot \frac{1}{2}(x-1)^{2} \\  & ={e}^{-1}-2{e}^{-1}(x-1)+{e}^{-1}(x-1)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

The second-degree Taylor polynomial of f(x)=e−x2 about x=1 is

a
e−1−2e−1(x−1)+e−1(x−1)2
b
−1+2e−1(x−1)+4e−1(x−1)2
c
e−1+e−1(x−1)+4e−1(x−1)2
d
e−1+e−1(x−1)−2e−1(x−1)2
e
1−2e−1(x−1)+e−1(x−1)2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the second-degree Taylor polynomial about x=1, we plug a=1 into the general formula to give

P2(x)=f(1)+f′(1)(x−1)+12f″(1)(x−1)2.

So, we need to work out f(1), f′(1), and f″(1):

f(x)=e−x2⟹f(1)=e−1f′(x)=−2xe−x2⟹f′(1)=−2e−1f″(x)=(4x2−2)e−x2⟹f″(1)=2e−1

We now plug the results for f(1), f′(1), and f″(1) into our second-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

P2(x)=e−1+(−2e−1)⋅(x−1)+(2e−1)⋅12(x−1)2=e−1−2e−1(x−1)+e−1(x−1)2.
